thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: HIGH latency spike + OOMs in us-west runtime pool detected. Alerts: 3 nodes flapped, multiple CUDA OOMs. Auto-escalation -> #eng-oncall.

Maya: seeing the alert, taking it. on-call Maya here — I’m paging SRE & runtime.

Raj: on it. looking at node metrics now, appear to be correlated with batcher queue growth on worker-23 / gpu-2.

Kevin: I’m pulling logs from the continuous-batcher on that host. can we reduce traffic routing to the pool?

Maya: routing change in progress — pausing new traffic to us-west:gpu-pool-3 via router flag.

deploy-bot: Router change applied by Maya — traffic diverted away from gpu-pool-3 (id: pool-3).

Anita: Customer support heads-up: Received 2 reports of elevated latency from customer_acme and 1 from customer_zephyr. They call it "responses timing out".

Raj: stack snapshot from node gpu-2 attached (snippet):
```
[2026-03-12T21:03:45Z] runtime: batcher queue length=11872, inflight batches=512
[2026-03-12T21:03:46Z] runtime: allocation failed: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY: failed to allocate 8388608 bytes
[2026-03-12T21:03:46Z] runtime: continuous_batcher blocked waiting for free slot, queue growth rate +600/s
[2026-03-12T21:03:47Z] kernel: process crash (sigsegv) pid=4321
```

Kevin: OOMs + queue growth => looks like continuous batcher deadlock/lockup under a sudden traffic surge. Could be a regression from the recent batching change (v2.8.1). I'll pull the runtime traces.

Maya: can we force drain or disable continuous batching on pool-3 to stop growth? We need fast mitigation.

Kevin: issuing kill -USR1 to batcher to force flush on those nodes now.

Kevin: done on gpu-2 — sending command:
```
ssh runtime@gpu-2 'pkill -USR1 continuous-batcher || true'
```

Raj: node responded, queue length decreased from ~11.8k -> 400 in ~18s. good. but we still saw two container restarts.

Kevin: flipping runtime flag to disable continuous batching for pool-3 temporarily.

Kevin: API call:
```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP" https://controlplane.internal/v1/flags -d '{"pool":"pool-3","continuous_batching":false}'
```

deploy-bot: Flag update succeeded (continuous_batching=false) for pool-3.

Maya: routing still paused, continuous batching disabled, nodes stabilizing. memory usage trending down.

Anita: CS update: customer_acme notified about degraded latency and mitigation in progress. ETA shared ~10-15m.

Raj: root cause hypothesis: the new batching policy increased max batch growth under high concurrency, allowing the queue to expand beyond paging threshold -> kernel OOMs when CUDA tried to allocate large KV caches. We need to check the batching policy change in the v2.8.1 rollout.

Kevin: I see an edge case in the growth limiter: if admitted concurrency spikes while backpressure signals not propagated due to socket timeouts, the queue admission code can accept unbounded prefixes. Fix is straightforward (enforce cap on total tokens in queue), but requires a runtime patch.

Maya: for immediate mitigation, do we want to scale pool-3 down to zero and re-schedule workloads to other regions? That will drop capacity but eliminate bad nodes.

Raj: prefer to cordon node gpu-2 and cordon pool-3 for further analysis. already cordoning.

Kevin: I’ll prepare a hotfix branch disabling the new admission ramp and cherry-pick to a canary build. Can we do a canary deploy to pool-1 (non-prod) first?

Maya: yes. Raj — can you confirm no further customer impact if we remove pool-3 from traffic and keep continuous_batching=false?

Raj: confirmed — SLOs for customers with reserved capacity may be impacted fallback -> they have fallback to dedicated nodes. I will update outages sheet.

Anita: Customers updated. CS asked to escalate to account team for customer_acme (high priority).

Kevin: pushing hotfix PR now: branch batcher-bounded-admit. PR: https://git.internal/runtime/pulls/4123

Kevin: test canary on staging pool-1 — no regressions locally. scheduling canary job.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for runtime v2.8.1-hotfix on pool-1 (non-prod).

Maya: handoff time — I need to go for 30m. Raj, Kevin you have the incident. Please update this thread with major state changes.

Raj: acknowledged, taking lead during Maya's break. will coordinate with Kevin on rollout.

Kevin: can confirm hotfix passes canary acceptance tests. Ready to roll to us-west but we should avoid simultaneous restarts across pools. Suggest rolling to one node at a time.

Raj: rolling to pool-3 disabled because cordoned. plan: uncordon with continuous_batching=false, drain node, apply hotfix, then re-enable traffic gradually. I’ll run the step sequence.

Maya: thanks. leaving a handoff note in the incident doc and updating #oncall-rotation.

Anita: logging incident ticket INC-2026-1675, customer impact: multi-tenant latency bump, 3 customers affected, no data loss.

Raj: current status summary (as of 1765554789): traffic routed away from pool-3, continuous_batching disabled for pool-3, queue lengths stabilized, kernel OOMs stopped, hotfix PR opened and canaried, support notified. severity: p2 (customer-visible, mitigated).

Kevin: follow-ups: 1) revert batching policy change or add admission cap, 2) add early paging threshold alarms (queue tokens > 5k), 3) add e2e test that simulates sudden concurrency spike.

Maya: good notes. I’ll pick up postmortem ownership once I’m back on shift. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
